cases.question: What was paid, why did implementation take time, and which judicial outcome now controls the captured record?
cases.finding: The September 2025 Supreme Court judgment records ₹19,350 crore paid to financial creditors and upholds the NCLAT resolution outcome. A debt haircut or delayed payment alone does not establish a political loan waiver.

claims.text: The Court records JSW paying ₹19,350 crore to financial creditors on 26 March 2021.
claims.response: Paragraph 114 records payment; the following paragraphs examine delay.
claims.alternative: Ordinary insolvency resolution trades full contractual debt recovery for going-concern value; this is not evidence of a government gift.
claims.falsifier: Bank-wise reconciliation differing from the recorded amount or a correcting court order would change the cash account.

claims.text: Open accounting question: did the approved bid terms and later creditor extension allocate operating surplus as agreed? The captured judgment rejects a late claim to redistribute EBITDA.
claims.response: Paragraphs 110–115 identify stays, clean-asset concerns and a creditor-approved extension. Paragraphs 186–190 reject late EBITDA claims under the approved terms.
claims.alternative: The recorded stays, clean-asset uncertainty and creditor-approved extension provide ordinary legal explanations. No new evidence of improper coordination was found.
claims.falsifier: The original bid terms, contemporaneous minutes and reconciled surplus ledger can resolve the allocation question. A lawful allocation consistent with the approved plan would close it without an adverse inference.

cases.title: Veteran training: DIAV, private facilitators and a prohibited subcontracting route
cases.question: Did the defence-skilling arrangement comply with PMKVY accreditation and subcontracting rules?
cases.period: July 2015 memorandum; PMKVY 1–3 audit; responses in 2023–2025
cases.finding: CAG records 1,843 candidates in 77 of 81 inspected training batches taught through third parties labelled IL&FS and Nidan Tech. The Ministry describes a selection committee; CAG maintains that the scheme prohibited subcontracting.

geography.label: New Delhi: ministry/DIAV administration
geography.basis: Administrative, institutional or asset association; not the location of a proven transfer or wrongdoing.

claims.text: CAG paragraph 3.4.1(b) identifies third-party delivery in 77 of 81 inspected batches despite the scheme prohibition on subcontracting.
claims.response: The Ministry said a constituted committee selected facilitators with NSDC and sector-council assistance; DIAV supplied mobilisation and infrastructure.
claims.alternative: Officials may have classified providers as facilitators rather than subcontractors. CAG nevertheless rejected the compliance explanation.
claims.falsifier: The signed memorandum, a valid rule exception and documented work scopes could change the contractual classification.

claims.text: Across the broader population of 264 centres, the audit identified two meeting all accreditation criteria and 38 with conditional accreditation.
claims.response: CAG states the memorandum and scheme requirements; footnote 30 explains conditional accreditation.
claims.alternative: Date mismatches or missing certificate links can misclassify centres. Conditional and unaccredited states must remain distinct.
claims.falsifier: Accreditation certificates valid for each batch date could change the eligibility assessment.
missingRecords: Centre accreditation history by batch date

whatWeKnow: No provider-specific payment amount was captured.
The 77-of-81 sample cannot be extrapolated to all 4,153 batches.
The label IL&FS does not resolve an exact legal entity.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Contract prices, actual payments and exact recipient companies.
Whether any training was fictitious; the selected paragraph does not establish that.

nextRecords.record: Contracts, legal identifiers and selection minutes
nextRecords.purpose: Resolve provider identity and the permitted contractual route.

nextRecords.record: Redacted batch payments and completion register
nextRecords.purpose: Join actual payments to accreditation and completion without publishing personal data.

limits: No operational military details or private beneficiary records are published.
The audit finding does not establish bribery or funding of attacks.

actors.incentive: Support resettlement subject to scheme rules
Meet delivery needs within contractual limits

informationThen: The memorandum is dated July 2015; the exact decision day was not established.
The audit describes permitted defence institutions and the requirement for accredited centres.

options.label: Use permitted accredited institutions
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Batch records linked to valid centre certificates

options.label: Select outside facilitators through a committee
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Signed work scopes and any applicable rule exception

decisionAnalysis.observedOutcome: Audit records accreditation and subcontracting concerns alongside the Ministry’s committee-selection explanation.
hindsightLimits: This is retrospective audit evidence, not an outcome known in 2015.
No dishonest intention is inferred from an institutional role or a provider name.

cases.title: Airport concessions and the later cost of temporary tariff relief
cases.question: Who received concession money, and who may bear a future tariff true-up after temporary airline relief?
cases.period: Concession context from 2019; receipts through 2022; April 2026 policy
cases.finding: The government reports concession receipts paid to AAI and later announces temporary tariff relief with a future under-recovery adjustment. Actual benefits and later user costs remain unmeasured. No favour or bribe is established.

claims.text: AAI reported receiving ₹710.88 crore in concession fees through October 2022 from the six concessionaires.
claims.response: The Ministry describes highest competitive bids and separately lists upfront payments.
claims.alternative: A concession transfers operating rights with contractual payment obligations; it is not necessarily an uncompensated transfer.
claims.falsifier: Audited fee ledgers inconsistent with the stated receipts would change this claim.

claims.text: Hypothesis: temporary relief may defer costs to future airport users if regulators allow under-recovery in later tariffs.
claims.response: The Ministry explicitly announces a later adjustment and relief across public and private airport settings.
claims.alternative: Ordinary regulated cost recovery can lawfully smooth cash flows. Traffic growth and other adjustments can offset the effect.
claims.falsifier: Final orders showing no such allowance or a net over-recovery would weaken the cost-shifting hypothesis.
missingRecords: Actual receipts and matched route-fare data

whatWeKnow: The April 2026 measure also covers AAI non-major airports.
Concession fees, airline charges and passenger fares are separate flows.
The stated West Asia crisis context does not establish responsibility for the crisis.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Airport-specific under-recovery and the later tariff adjustment.
Whether airlines passed savings to passengers.
Any covert corporate–ministry exchange; none is established.

nextRecords.purpose: Measure authorised timing and allocation of costs.
Reconcile awards with cash receipts and enforcement.

cases.title: Delhi airport: tariffs, dollar maturities and a reported rupee refinancing
cases.question: Can published tariff requests be joined to debt maturities and later financing without mistaking lobbying for wrongdoing?
cases.sector: transport / foreign debt / public and private finance / regulation
cases.period: 2016 bond context; February 2025 proposal; September–October 2026 refinancing records
cases.finding: DIAL explicitly linked its request for earlier regulated revenue to refinancing dollar debt. CARE later rated a proposed ₹3,500 crore issue, and October reporting names subscribers. Settlement, redemption and ultimate investor identities are not verified.

geography.label: Delhi International Airport
geography.basis: Administrative, institutional or asset association; not the location of a proven transfer or wrongdoing.

geography.label: Mumbai: capital markets association
geography.basis: Administrative, institutional or asset association; not the location of a proven transfer or wrongdoing.

claims.text: DIAL’s February 2025 letter requests earlier CP4 revenue, citing a rounded US$522 million maturity and refinancing needs.
claims.response: The operator argues for viability within total allowed CP4 revenue and requests roughly ₹450 per passenger in FY2025-26 and FY2026-27.
claims.alternative: Lawful regulation of capital-intensive infrastructure can align cash generation and debt service. A request does not prove capture.
claims.falsifier: The final tariff order and stakeholder analysis could show the request was rejected, modified or justified by allowed costs.
missingRecords: Final CP4 tariff order and calculation model

claims.text: CARE rates a proposed ₹3,500 crore issue; ET later reports completion and subscribers. Original settlement evidence remains missing.
claims.response: The rating identifies refinancing risk and mitigating factors. ET attributes transaction details to unnamed sources.
claims.alternative: Ordinary currency and maturity refinancing can reduce risk. Proposal, allotment and settlement dates can differ.
claims.falsifier: Allotment, trustee and redemption records would confirm or contradict the reported sequence.

claims.text: Hypothesis: earlier regulated revenue could shift financing costs to current passengers without a corresponding benefit.
claims.response: The company reports improved results after tariff changes; CARE recognises regulatory true-ups and asset strength.
claims.alternative: Financing stability may benefit service continuity. A year-on-year profit change does not isolate the effect of tariffs.
claims.falsifier: A complete discounted tariff model and service-cost comparison showing neutrality or user benefits would weaken the adverse hypothesis.

whatWeKnow: The operator’s published request makes the debt–tariff connection explicit.
ET names IIFCL, NIIF Infrastructure Finance, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, IDFC First Bank and SBI Capital Markets. These remain one unverified reporting group.
Dollar face value, a rupee carrying balance and new bond face value are different measures and cannot be added.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Actual October 2026 settlement and dollar-bond redemption.
The final regulator’s reasoning on the requested timing of revenue.
Private agreements or political links; none are inferred.

Verify retirement of the dollar debt.

nextRecords.purpose: Determine which requests were actually allowed.

limits: CARE supplies an issuer-paid credit opinion. The reported subscriptions still require primary transaction evidence.
No bribe, default or public bailout is established.

actors.incentive: Explicit goal: support refinancing and the credit rating

informationThen: DIAL reported past losses, expansion expenditure and an October 2026 debt maturity.
Only the operator’s information packet was captured; the regulator’s internal analysis remains unknown.

options.expectedObservableOutcome: More near-term cash; test present-value effects and financing terms

options.expectedObservableOutcome: A larger near-term financing requirement, observable in loan terms

decisionAnalysis.observedOutcome: The company later reported revised tariffs and improved quarterly results. A September rating and October report indicate refinancing steps, not independently verified redemption.
hindsightLimits: Later outcomes are not used as February 2025 prediction features.
Options are testable mechanisms; no invented payoff or personal intent is assigned.
